items.name: docketscraper
items.description: The client is required to scrape specific data from legal cases filed within 2020 from a website storing legal cases. The homepage of the website consists of a search bar where the cities can be searched. The client provided a list of cities that needed to be scrapped. Even though the task looks straightforward, it required an automation step to search the city from the search bar. Furthermore, the information required to be scraped were stored inside tables that did not follow a specific pattern. The automation part of the task was achieved using the selenium web driver. Using the web driver the city name was passed into the search bar. Then the search result page was scraped using BeautifulSoup library to get the docket numbers of each legal case. Using the regular expression library, the docket numbers of the cases filed in 2020 were selected. This was possible because the docket number format consists of the year in which the case was filed. Upon selecting the docket numbers, the links to each case were obtained. Each link was saved into a python list.  Then the web pages corresponding to the links were loaded using the Python requests library.  The final output was saved as an excel file with sheets corresponding to each city in the list provided by the client. Python functions were written to each stage of the program.

items.name: Energy-Radar
items.description: No single tool tracks U.S. energy projects. The data is scattered across grid queues, dockets, permits, and news. Worse, projects change LLC names at every stage. Building a full picture today means hopping between five websites and guessing if different filings belong to the same project.
